sessions.session_title: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting (Matt Carlisle)
sessions.transcript_text:
She’Lah attended his scheduled Resource Navigation appointment today, marking his first appointment since being terminated from the program last month. He had previously missed two scheduled Resource Navigation appointments with DiYoung without notice. However, he reestablished contact last week following a rearrest for CDV 3rd offense. He was subsequently released and placed on home detention pending his court date. He also remains on probation related to prior charges from his previous incarceration.

During today’s appointment, She’Lah expressed interest in discussing the possibility of returning to the program. We reviewed the expectations and conditions that would need to be met before reconsideration for returning to the program. First, he agreed to attend weekly check-in appointments with me and submit to urinalysis testing as part of ongoing accountability and monitoring.

We also discussed the importance of securing reliable transportation. She’Lah acknowledged that he currently lacks a dependable transportation plan. He was advised that establishing consistent transportation would be necessary to support regular attendance and participation in program activities. Specifically, relying on rides from various female acquaintances or attempting to arrange transportation through other program participants would not be considered a sufficient or sustainable plan.

A significant portion of the discussion focused on his identified risk factors, particularly peer influence and interpersonal relationships. She’Lah acknowledged that these areas have contributed to past difficulties and demonstrated an awareness of the need to make meaningful changes in his choices, relationships, and behavior moving forward.

As an action step before our next appointment, She’Lah was instructed to identify and establish a reliable transportation plan. He agreed to work toward this goal and return next week on the same day and at the same time for his next scheduled check-in. Continued progress toward meeting these expectations will be considered as part of any future decision regarding program reentry.

sessions.session_title: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting (Diyoung Dantzler)
sessions.transcript_text:
Shelah demonstrated increased insight into his personal risk factors and how his decisions can affect his progress\. He was able to identify that being mindful of his surroundings and considering how others may perceive his reactions can help him avoid unnecessary consequences\. He acknowledged that he sometimes gives himself excuses for small mistakes and identified the importance of setting boundaries with himself and making more responsible decisions\. Shelah continues to use his free time constructively by searching for employment opportunities on Indeed and remains focused on obtaining stable employment and transportation\.

**Barriers:**
Shelah arrived late Monday following his previous suspension related to difficulty managing his emotions while speaking on the phone in a public parking area\. Transportation continues to be a barrier despite Shelah recently obtaining his driver’s license\. He acknowledged that he has not consistently followed through with available transportation resources, including Dial\-A\-Ride, and identified forgetfulness as a factor that can interfere with following through\. He also recognized that becoming comfortable or making excuses for small issues could potentially lead to larger consequences, including stagnation or procrastination toward his goals\.

**Goals:**
Shelah’s immediate goal is to obtain a job interview with a company located close enough to reduce transportation difficulties and expenses while he works toward obtaining his own vehicle\. He also identified the need to become more consistent with transportation planning, follow through with available resources, arrive on time, and continue developing emotional self\-control and personal accountability\.

**Intervention:**
Case manager used motivational interviewing and accountability\-based questioning to help Shelah examine the connection between his decisions, consequences, and long\-term goals\. Shelah was asked what he could have done differently regarding the previous phone incident\. He identified that he could have ended the conversation and addressed the matter after work rather than risk his employment by reacting publicly\.

Following his late arrival Monday, Shelah was held accountable and informed that continued lateness could jeopardize his participation\. Discussion focused on the importance of communicating when circumstances may cause him to be late and taking proactive steps to prevent transportation problems\. Shelah identified that he could arrange transportation ahead of time or contact staff for assistance\.

Case manager revisited the previously provided Dial\-A\-Ride resource after Shelah acknowledged that he had not followed through with using it\. Through discussion, Shelah recognized that failing to utilize available resources could lead to discouragement and reinforce the belief that things are not working for him\. He identified forgetfulness as an area that he needs to address\.

Case manager also explored Shelah’s understanding of personal risk factors and accountability\. Shelah stated that learning about his risk factors surprised him because he had not previously recognized how certain habits and behaviors were contributing to problems in his life\. He acknowledged that having knowledge is not enough and that he must apply what he is learning to his daily decisions\.

Shelah was encouraged to view accountability as an opportunity for growth rather than a reason to give up\. He identified that accountability can help him become more responsible and avoid developing tunnel vision\. He also recognized the importance of using his free time constructively and preparing ahead of time for potential transportation issues\.

**Next Steps:**

- Shelah will contact Dial\-A\-Ride before 10:00 a\.m\. to begin utilizing the transportation resource provided\.
- Shelah will plan transportation in advance rather than waiting until the last minute\.
- Shelah will communicate with staff as soon as possible when an unexpected transportation issue occurs\.
- Shelah will continue using Indeed and other employment resources to seek employment\.
- Shelah’s goal for the week is to obtain an interview with a company located close to him to reduce transportation barriers and expenses\.
- Shelah will continue working toward obtaining reliable personal transportation and eventually a vehicle\.
- Shelah will continue practicing emotional regulation, personal accountability, and following through with available support resources\.
- Case management will continue monitoring punctuality, transportation follow\-through, employment progress, and Shelah’s ability to apply knowledge of his personal risk factors to daily decision\-making\.

sessions.session_title: Check-in conversation – brief status update (Matt Carlisle)
sessions.transcript_text:
Had a conversation with She’Lah this morning regarding recent attendance and behavioral concerns.  She’Lah was sent home by DiYoung on Friday due to disruptive behavior.  Despite this, he arrived late this morning and left the Q1 class to go to the parking lot to retrieve food that someone had dropped off for him.

This is She’Lah’s fifth week in the program. He has been late three times due to transportation issues (9/3, 9/9, and 9/21).  I explained to She’Lah that if he is late again or misses another day, we would need to transition him back to Resource Navigation until his circumstances are more stable and he is able to consistently meet the expectations of the program.

sessions.session_title: Behavioral incident – disruption, conflict, or left early (Diyoung Dantzler)
sessions.transcript_text:
Shelah took accountability for his actions and was able to identify how his behavior affected his progress. He recognized that he needs to be more mindful of how he responds to emotional situations, especially in public and at work.

Barriers

Shelah had difficulty managing his emotions while speaking with a family member on the phone during lunch. He was shouting loudly in a public parking lot, which resulted in him being held accountable, asked to go home, and suspended for Friday.

Goals

Shelah’s goal is to improve his emotional regulation, think before reacting, and avoid behaviors that could negatively affect his employment and progress toward his long-term goals.

Intervention

I used accountability-based questioning by asking Shelah what he could have done differently. Shelah identified that he needs to be more mindful of having emotional family conversations while at work because family conflict can trigger unexpected and difficult emotions.

Next Steps

Shelah plans to pause and think before reacting, especially when dealing with family-related stress. He will work on managing his emotions appropriately in public and at work to prevent setbacks and continue moving forward toward his goals

sessions.session_title: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting (Diyoung Dantzler)
sessions.transcript_text:
Strengths

Shelah continues to show increased awareness of the behaviors and thought patterns that support his goals. He identified the importance of balancing discipline and motivation and allowing himself time to respond rather than react to unexpected situations. He recognizes how easily he can be pulled back into old patterns and is working toward developing healthier behaviors.

Shelah has also been making progress in rebuilding his relationship with his daughter. He recognizes the importance of understanding her feelings and being intentional about strengthening their relationship. He identified his current support system as an important influence in helping him remain focused and accountable.

Barriers

Shelah continues to struggle with accepting help from others because he prefers to handle things independently and does not like feeling indebted to anyone. He acknowledged that refusing assistance can sometimes create unnecessary barriers and close doors to opportunities. He is working on recognizing that not everyone has negative intentions when offering support.

He also identified limited time during the day to handle important responsibilities, particularly with businesses and services closing before he is finished with programming. He understands that employment will need to provide a healthy transition that allows him to continue managing these responsibilities.

Shelah remains undecided about a specific career path because he has not yet explored all of his talents and interests. He also acknowledged that managing setbacks independently can become overwhelming and may lead to the “F-it” mentality.

Goals

* Continue developing discipline and consistency in his daily routine.
* Break old behavioral patterns and practice responding instead of reacting.
* Strengthen his relationship with his daughter.
* Complete his OSHA certification and forklift certification.
* Obtain his driver’s license or schedule the required appointment.
* Continue working with Vocational Rehabilitation for additional support.
* Explore career options based on his skills, interests, and talents.
* Improve financial literacy and understanding of basic economics.
* Develop strategies for managing setbacks without returning to old behaviors.
* Build a support system and become more comfortable accepting appropriate help.

Intervention

Case management focused on helping Shelah identify the connection between discipline, motivation, decision-making, and maintaining new behaviors. Discussion explored how creating a pause before responding to unexpected situations can prevent him from returning to old patterns.

Shelah was encouraged to examine his current influences, how he spends his free time, and whether those influences support or interfere with his goals. We also discussed the importance of accepting appropriate support and understanding that receiving help does not necessarily create a debt or obligation.

Case management also reinforced the importance of time management, completing responsibilities before the end of the day, and developing a realistic employment plan that supports his transition. Shelah completed his first meeting with Vocational Rehabilitation and is seeking additional assistance.

Next Steps

Shelah will work toward scheduling or completing his driver’s license appointment, continue his OSHA and forklift certifications, and follow up with Vocational Rehabilitation regarding additional resources. He will also explore potential career fields and identify at least one area of interest to begin researching.

Shelah will continue practicing the difference between reacting and responding, accepting appropriate support, managing setbacks, and maintaining accountability to his goals. He will also continue working on strengthening his relationship with his daughter and using his current support system to remain focused and productive.

sessions.session_title: Coaching / case management session – structured or in-depth meeting (Diyoung Dantzler)
sessions.transcript_text:
Presenting Needs & Progress:
Shelah reported positive engagement with the program and stated that he appreciates the opportunities and doors the program provides. He identified improvement in his problem-solving and ability to handle life matters more effectively. He demonstrated increased insight into the importance of discipline, stating that motivation can come and go, while discipline requires doing what needs to be done regardless of how he feels.

Employment/Career Goals:
Shelah identified construction as his desired career field, with specific interest in roofing, painting, and drywall. He is also pursuing his CDL and has already completed a permit test. Staff discussed connecting him with Goodwill and Vocational Rehabilitation for assistance with CDL training and employment opportunities. Shelah expressed confidence in developing a long-term career and creating a legacy for his family.

Emotional Regulation/Risk Management:
Shelah demonstrated insight into situations that may trigger anger, particularly interactions with authority figures. He identified physical warning signs of anger, including feeling his body temperature increase and his face becoming hot. He acknowledged that his past experiences can influence his reactions to individuals wearing badges or carrying radios. Through discussion, he identified respectful and assertive communication as an alternative to walking away, becoming confrontational, or making impulsive decisions.

Family/Personal Development:
Shelah identified strengthening his relationship with his daughter as a major priority. His six-month goal is to establish a stable living situation and consistent daily routine that allows him to be more present and supportive in her life. He also wants to improve his ability to understand and respond to her emotions. He expressed strong confidence in his personal growth and stated that returning to his previous way of life is no longer an option for him.

Financial Goal:
Shelah identified saving $75 toward obtaining his driver’s license as his immediate weekly commitment.

MI Intervention:
Staff used open-ended questions, reflective listening, affirmation, and discrepancy exploration to help Shelah connect his current choices with his long-term goals. Discussion focused on discipline, emotional awareness, respectful communication, family responsibility, career development, and building a positive legacy. Shelah was encouraged to identify specific behaviors he can control rather than focusing on circumstances outside of his control.

Accountability / Action Steps:

1. Save $75 toward obtaining his driver’s license.
2. Follow up with Vocational Rehabilitation regarding his CDL-school appointment.
3. Explore Goodwill/CDL employment-training resources.
4. Apply for construction-related employment opportunities.
5. Practice recognizing physical signs of anger before responding.
6. Use respectful, assertive communication when disagreeing with authority figures.
7. Continue working toward improved communication and consistency with his daughter.

Case Management Assessment:
Shelah appears motivated toward positive change and demonstrates growing self-awareness regarding emotional regulation, career development, financial responsibility, and family relationships. His primary areas for continued development are impulse control, managing reactions to authority, maintaining discipline, and consistently following through on identified goals. Continued accountability and reinforcement of his strengths are recommended.

sessions.transcript_text:
Shalah Norman presented as a walk-in for case management services. He successfully completed and passed his drug screening. He reports having a supportive relationship with his mother and currently resides with her, providing stable housing. He is currently on two years of probation supervision.

Goals

Shalah identified several important goals for his next stage of reentry and personal development:

* Obtain his driver’s license.
* Continue pursuing CDL education and certification with the goal of entering the trucking industry.
* Strengthen and maintain a positive relationship with his 11-year-old daughter.
* Remain connected to positive guidance, support, and accountability.
* Maintain sobriety and continue making responsible decisions.
* Explore employment opportunities while working toward his long-term career goal.

Education & Employment

Shalah reports that he has obtained his GED and has already begun preparing for the CDL process. He recently completed a CDL-related preparation test and expressed interest in pursuing trucking as a career. He is open to employment opportunities that can provide a starting point while he works toward obtaining his CDL.

Strengths & Support System

Shalah identified his mother as a source of support and reports having reliable transportation to attend appointments and program activities. He demonstrated insight into personal accountability, stating that he believes problems often begin with how he responds to situations. He recognizes the importance of stepping away from conflict, managing anger, and taking responsibility for his choices.

Areas of Focus

Case management will continue to support Shalah with obtaining his driver’s license, connecting him with CDL training and possible funding resources, developing employment opportunities, strengthening family relationships, and maintaining positive guidance and accountability.

Case Manager Assessment

Shalah appears motivated to improve his circumstances and establish a productive career path. His immediate priorities are obtaining his driver’s license and pursuing CDL certification. Continued case management support, positive guidance, employment assistance, and accountability are recommended to help him remain focused on his goals and successfully progress through reentry.

Next Steps

The next case management meeting should review progress toward obtaining his driver’s license, CDL enrollment, employment opportunities, relationship-building with his daughter, and continued compliance with probation and program expectations.
